title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

reading.body:
This incident involves the sustained, deliberate impersonation of a real person online, carried out over years using fake videos and AI-generated imagery. The AI component was one tool among several used to produce fabricated pornographic material and to deceive men into believing they were in contact with Fernandes. The deployment here was not a commercial AI system gone wrong in the conventional sense, but AI image and video generation used as an instrument of targeted harassment and identity fraud against a specific individual.

The failure is not a model asserting a false fact or a system deployed without oversight in a corporate setting. It is the use of generative AI tools to manufacture non-consensual intimate imagery, a use case that sits outside any intended deployment condition but that the tools were technically capable of enabling. Detection depended entirely on the victim's own investigative effort over years, not on any platform or provider mechanism catching the misuse.

What is not established is that Fernandes's allegation against her former husband has been proven, adjudicated, or confirmed by any independent investigation, and the reporting does not establish his guilt as a finding of fact.

reports.title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.

summary:
German actress and television personality Collien Fernandes discovered that someone had been impersonating her online for years, engaging in sexually explicit affairs with men and distributing pornographic material purporting to show her. The harassment included fake videos, AI-generated imagery, and people charging money for alleged access to her. After years of receiving little help, Fernandes decided to investigate the impersonators herself like a journalist would, working to identify who was behind the deception. By March 2026, she believed she had finally found one person responsible and prepared to publicly expose them.

Fernandes had recently divorced Christian Ulmen, a famous German actor and comedian known for his humor centered on embarrassment and humiliation. During their 14-year marriage, the couple was highly visible in German media and were often portrayed as a modern, egalitarian partnership with strong feminist values. Fernandes had become known for advocating against double standards for working mothers and for her work promoting gender equality through children's books and a documentary about feminism, making her investigation and exposure of her impersonator particularly significant in sparking a larger feminist movement.
